title: Invertible oplax comparisons define a strong monoidal structure
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category] equipped with monoidal structures [def-sfb-monoidal-category], that is, tensor bifunctors, unit objects $\mathbf 1_{\mathcal C},\mathbf 1_{\mathcal D}$, and natural associator and left and right unitor isomorphisms satisfying the pentagon and triangle identities. Let $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor, equipped with an oplax monoidal structure: a map $d_0:L\mathbf 1_{\mathcal C}\to\mathbf 1_{\mathcal D}$ and natural maps $d_{X,Y}:L(X\otimes Y)\to LX\otimes LY$ satisfying the oplax associativity and the two unit identities. Suppose $d_0$ and every $d_{X,Y}$ are isomorphisms. Then $L$ has the strong monoidal structure [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] with lax unit $d_0^{-1}:\mathbf 1_{\mathcal D}\to L\mathbf 1_{\mathcal C}$ and lax tensor maps $d_{X,Y}^{-1}:LX\otimes LY\to L(X\otimes Y)$; its oplax comparison maps are the given $d_0,d_{X,Y}$.
